chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you intend to supplicate, glorify Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and praise Him, and glorify Him, and extol Him, and laud upon Him, and send blessings upon Muhammad the Prophet and his Progeny, then ask, you will be given.'

key_terms.سَبِّحْهُ: Glory to Him / Declare Him free from imperfection
key_terms.هَلِّلْهُ: Extol Him / Say La ilaha illallah

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette and opening formula for making a supplication in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the canonical structure of Islamic supplication, emphasizing that honoring God through specific acts of glorification (tasbih, hamd, tahlil) and invoking the Prophet and Ahl al-Bayt serves as a spiritual prerequisite for acceptance. In Shia tradition, this sequence reflects the principle that dua is not merely a request but a relational dialogue where acknowledging divine majesty and prophetic intercession prepares the heart for receiving grace.
